newsitem.title: USA: Wet conditions continue to slow Oklahoma harvest.
newsitem.headline: Wet conditions continue to slow Oklahoma harvest.

text.p: Wet conditions during the week ended Sunday continued to slow harvesting of Oklahoma's row crops, the weekly state crop report said.

Cotton harvest made good progress during the week until rains brought it to a halt. Freezing temperatures along with ice and rain have caused many areas of peanuts to be abandoned in south central Oklahoma.

Wheat condition continues to be rated mostly good statewide, although yellowing of wheat stems and rust have been reported in many fields across the state. Excess rains caused some floods in fields in southeast Oklahoma.
Wheat was 29 percent grazed, compared to 21 percent a week ago, eight percent a year ago and 21 percent on a five-year average.
Wheat was rated 84 percent good to excellent, vs 83 at that level last week.
Sorghum harvested 95 percent vs 86 w/a, 94 y/a, 91 avg.
Soybeans harvested 91 percent vs 90 w/a, 94 y/a, 89 avg.
Cotton harvested 51 percent vs 41 w/a, 74 y/a, 67 avg.
Cotton rated 28 percent good/excellent, vs 28 last week.
Pasture and range condition rated 73 percent good to excellent vs 70 last week.
